transcript: Let's talk about the controversial play that just opened off Broadway, Prince F. A play so provocative that I literally cannot say the title of this play without getting demonetized. The debate around this play has really been regarding its subject matter, as this play is based on this photograph of the real life Prince George when he was four years old. And when that photo came out, you had a lot of people speculating that that pose is very queer coded, and therefore George could be gay. And that incident inspired this play, which takes it one step further and imagines a fictional future for Prince George in which he is an out gay man, specifically portraying him with a sexual proclivity for BDSM and portraying several graphic sex scenes. And while they are quick to point out that this play is not really about George specifically as much as it is about a broader queer experience, I do understand where a lot of the criticism is coming from. Like, putting aside the fact that he is currently a child, the fact that they are writing and portraying these graphic sex scenes of someone who is very much a real person. It's just kind of weird to me. Like, if someone wrote a play like this about me that imagined what kind of sex I like and depicted it in graphic detail, whether that sex was gay, straight, doesn't really matter, I would feel kind of uncomfortable about that. And maybe That makes me a prude. I don't know. But I do find it kind of weird, which is a shame, because that aspect aside, this is actually a very good play. Because, like I said, this is largely a play about the queer experience. And the questions that it raises and the themes that it explores are genuinely really interesting. But I also think it would be just as effective if you changed all the names and made it a hypothetical royal family.
